I've written round 400. It fixes the C bug from round 399 (C-R399-01) and finishes PERF-14b-i. The decision is **CONTINUE**. I didn't touch any app or store source: the store diff hash is the same as when A finished round 399.

**What went wrong in round 399.** It was my spec error. One rule said "scroll the target clip into view before reading it", and another said "every measured value must equal the published baseline (`c3ee1d6`)". For the Ctrl+D copy in the group-drag test, both can't hold: the copy sits about 4000 px off-screen even now, and scrolling while playing pauses Follow. A stopped correctly, and C confirmed the STOP in the browser. Gate 399 was skipped, so A's other round-399 work stays in the tree, unpublished.

**The ruling for the copy:**
- **Copy on screen** (always true today): it is read directly, with no scroll. Today's results therefore can't change.
- **Copy unmounted** (only with the planned clip virtualization): the harness scrolls next to the original, reads, and scrolls back. This happens only outside the measured windows, and Follow is turned back on if the scroll paused it.
- **Before the drag starts:** it uses a reading taken during setup, so it never scrolls there.
- **During the drag:** it doesn't read an unmounted copy. That one check (f) is skipped, and check (c) still proves the copy moved after release.
- **New check (g):** Follow must be on when the drag starts during playback.

**Evidence before dispatch.** I wrote the change as a patch and ran the interactions perf spec alone on two scratch copies of the current tree:
- **Current tree:** all 189 deterministic rows equal the baseline, with no problems in any of the 6 passes.
- **With the virtualization sketch:** no problems in any pass, every row has samples, and group-drag liveness is 1. The only failing check is `path-rewrites` (2 against a budget of 3), a known effect of virtualization that the next stage will re-rule.

**Review.** `tech-lead` reviewed the patch and found one High: after a failed copy read, the function returned early, which could hide a failure behind a liveness of 1. It also found a Medium in the scroll-restore check. I fixed both and re-ran both trees with the same results. The second Medium is that check (f) never runs under virtualization; I kept that as a recorded deviation. `tech-lead` did not see the fixes, so A must run `code-reviewer` on the applied change this round.

**Round 400 scope:**
- A may change only the interactions spec (applying my patch byte-for-byte) and doc 255. Everything else from round 399 is frozen at its current hash.
- C runs the full set of checks this time, including the resources and scale specs that C skipped in round 399.

**Schedule change.** I moved RETRO from round 400 to round 401. A RETRO on a tree that still holds unverified changes would have no clean point to publish. It's a one-round slip, recorded in the backlog. The next regression round is due on or after 2026-11-10.

**Recorded, not scheduled:**
- Inputs for the virtualization stage: the `path-rewrites` row; `res.harness.clips-1` still counting DOM clips; and a new question, whether clips moved as part of a group should stay mounted during the drag.
- The reviewers' Low findings went to `deferred_low_polish`.
- The root architecture checkpoint (ARCH-CHECKPOINT-PREVIEW-AFTER-13C) is still due and doesn't block.

I consulted the advisor twice: before writing, and at the review stage. That second call caught two clauses in my task that contradicted each other; they're now one rule. It also caught that the sketch had no review yet, which led to the `tech-lead` run. Nothing new is ready for root to publish until C passes round 400.
